findings.F1: The book's loss comes from its short side. Short trades lost at every holding length: 214 trades of up to 5 days summed -387.8 %, 56 of 6 to 10 days -122.9 %, and 52 of 10 to 30 days -199.9 %. Long trades held longer than 5 days gained: 11 trades at 5 to 6 days +90.6 %, 57 at 6 to 10 days +148.7 %, 58 at 10 to 30 days +106.4 %. Per bar in a position, short positions earned -0.019 % on 688 bars and long positions +0.021 % on 830 bars.
findings.F2: Over 5 days, only up days follow through, and the follow-through grows with the size of the day. On all bars, the 5-day excess return in the day's direction rises with the day's size in 30-day swing units (|z|) after up days, with slope +0.0162 (t 2.18, 610 non-overlapping cases), but not after down days, with slope -0.0002 (t -0.03, 754 cases). Up days with |z| > 1.5 were followed by a mean of +3.94 % (t 2.26, 72 cases), down days with |z| > 1.5 by -0.33 % (t -0.29, 75 cases).
findings.F3: The follow-through is stronger in agitated markets than in calm ones, against the brief's claim. Agitated here means the 30-day swing is above its own 120-day median, a proxy for the profile's swing measure. Over 5 days, the graded slope was +0.0548 (t 3.00, 138 cases) after agitated down days and +0.0356 (t 1.99, 122 cases) after agitated up days. In calm markets the slopes were -0.0100 (t -1.36, 616 cases) after down days and +0.0109 (t 1.35, 488 cases) after up days.
findings.F4: In calm markets, a down day that is large against the coin's swing is followed by a rebound that grows with the size of the day. The graded slope of the move in the day's direction was -0.0077 over 2 days (t -2.60, 1391 cases), -0.0100 over 5 days (t -1.36, 616 cases) and -0.0298 over 10 days (t -2.09, 314 cases). After calm up days the slopes were +0.0017 over 2 days (t 0.60) and +0.0135 over 10 days (t 0.86), neither distinguishable from zero.
findings.F5: In choppy markets (60-day return between -10 % and +10 %), up days continue clearly over 5 days and down days do not. The graded slope was +0.0612 after up days (t 2.67, 64 cases) and -0.0008 after down days (t -0.02, 61 cases). In the tested profile, up days with |z| > 1.5 in a choppy calm market were followed by +6.16 % (t 2.57, 7 cases).
findings.F6: Next-day excess returns differ by weekday. Thursday averaged +0.41 % (t 2.81, 1190 days) and Friday +0.38 % (t 2.76, 1182 days); Wednesday averaged -0.50 % (t -2.78, 1202 days). This overlaps the held idea 045-01 (rising market late week gain), so it is not a discovery.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's one-day rise against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days, the further it keeps rising over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader follows large up days on the long side only, sized by the day's size in swing units, and does not short large down days.
ideas.name: big up day continues

ideas.idea: In an agitated market, the larger a coin's one-day move against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days, the further it keeps moving in that day's direction over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader follows large days in the day's direction when the coin has been swinging more than usual, sized by the day's size in swing units.
ideas.name: agitated big day continues

ideas.idea: In a calm market, the larger a coin's one-day fall against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days, the more it rises back over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader buys large down days in quiet markets, sized by the fall's size in swing units, instead of following them.
ideas.name: calm big fall rebounds
